text: im curious, and likely isnt (but could be) the problem, but for what reason do we return values to the javascript? is there a reason why? or is it 'just because' ?
resolution: Answered the follow-up on why topology doors return values to JavaScript. Verified in v8_bindings_core.zig that every topology door returns {ok,key,count} JSON synchronously to its caller and the new key rides no push channel. Explanation delivered: there IS a principled reason JS holds the key — React declares the scene (<Scene3D.Mesh hostKey>) so it must hold the NAME of what to draw; that part is the framework's declarative contract, not incidental. But the returned string fuses two jobs: document identity (which React genuinely needs) and generation/cache-epoch (a host-internal cache concern that leaked into the JS contract), and the delivery is the natural-but-incidental shape of a function call — the one caller becomes the postman who must relay the new generation to every other consumer. Flagged that this IS plausibly the root of the adoption-failure class, and named the two structural fixes (stable per-document handle with host-internal generation rebinding, or broadcasting key changes on the existing event ring). No code changed — explanation only.
